newsitem.title: UK: Asia-Pacific passenger traffic to triple by 2010.
newsitem.headline: Asia-Pacific passenger traffic to triple by 2010.

text.p: Air passenger traffic to, from and within the Asia-Pacific region is forecast to nearly triple to 393 million passengers a year by 2010 from 134 million at present, an International Air Transport Association (IATA) report said.
Two-thirds of this travel will be entirely within the region, IATA added.
It said that rapid economic growth, expanding regional and long-haul tourism as well as the intensification of intra-Asian trade are three key reasons for the steep increase in journeys by air.

A summary of IATA's latest "Asia Pacific Air Transport Forecast:1980-2010" issued here includes forecasts up to 2010 from the present as well as historical data going back in some cases to 1980, an IATA official said.

The report added that between 1995 and 2010, Asia-Pacific international scheduled passenger traffic will rise at a projected average annual rate of 7.4 percent, while that for the rest of the world will grow at 4.4 percent annual average.
The global share of Asia-Pacific international scheduled passenger will increase to 49.8 percent by 2010 from 35.2 percent in 1995, IATA added. In 1985 this share was for 26.2 percent.

North East Asia -- which includes Japan, China (and Hong Kong), Korea and Taiwan will grow in importance as a source and destination for air travel, accounting for half of all intercontinental trips within to or from Asia-Pacific and over 70 percent of trips within the region, IATA said.
